record.original_question: Prove that if a 2n-dimensional manifold M^{2n} with n > 2 admits an almost complex structure, then M^{2n} also admits an integrable complex structure.

evidence.quote: Prove that if M^{2n} (n>2) admits an almost complex structure, then it also admits an integrable one

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M^{2n}$ be a smooth, connected, closed (compact without boundary) manifold of real dimension $2n$ with $n>2$. An almost complex structure on $M^{2n}$ is a smooth bundle endomorphism $J : TM \to TM$ of the tangent bundle satisfying $J^2 = -\mathrm{Id}$. Such a $J$ is said to be integrable if it is induced by an underlying complex-analytic structure on $M^{2n}$; equivalently, by the Newlander–Nirenberg theorem, if its Nijenhuis tensor
$$N_J(X,Y) = [X,Y] + J[JX,Y] + J[X,JY] - [JX,JY]$$
vanishes identically for all smooth vector fields $X,Y$ on $M^{2n}$.

Prove or disprove: every smooth closed manifold $M^{2n}$ with $n>2$ that admits some almost complex structure also admits an integrable complex structure (not necessarily homotopic to the given one).
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of whether every closed almost complex manifold of real dimension $2n$ with $n>2$ admits an integrable complex structure is widely regarded as open. Even the most famous test case, the 6-sphere $S^6$, remains unresolved as of recent surveys. While Gromov–Landweber-type results handle the open (non-compact) case, no comparable criterion exists for compact manifolds.

status_evidence.title: Almost complex manifold — Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In 1951 Steenrod conjectured that not every almost complex manifold admits a complex analytic structure; the existence question in higher dimensions remains highly subtle.
status_evidence.claim: The general existence question for integrable complex structures on almost complex manifolds is open.

status_evidence.title: Topological aspects of complex and almost complex manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Whether the 6-sphere $S^6$ admits an integrable complex structure is a long-standing open problem.
status_evidence.claim: The 6-dimensional case (S^6) is still open, illustrating that the general question for n>2 is open.
